checks.analysis: The output is the literal finite sum over P.support of C(P.coeff d) times ksBalancedDescentPolynomial(d0,d1,d2,d3). It retains each original complex coefficient exactly, without replacing it by a norm or conjugate. The support is the original input polynomial support, so each original nonzero monomial contributes once; polynomial arithmetic handles output collisions and cancellation.

The input variable order is (z1,z2,w1,w2), while the output variable order is (X0,X1,X2,r), despite both using Fin 4. The exponents are passed in input order d0,d1,d2,d3 to the previously reviewed pairing and literal polynomial. There is no identification of physical variables with input spinor variables.

Homogeneity of degree m explicitly requires both balanced support d0+d1=d2+d3 and uniform row degree d0+d1=m, only for d in P.support. Each summand has IsHomogeneous m by the monomial theorem and multiplication by a constant; the finite-sum closure proves the target. No output nonzero or exact totalDegree equality is asserted. If P=0 both support hypotheses are vacuous and the output zero polynomial is correctly homogeneous in every degree.

Physical evaluation requires balanced support alone, so sums containing several balanced degrees are included. The proof expands the actual input evaluation as the sum of P.coeff d times the product over all four input variables, maps evaluation over the output finite sum, and uses the exact monomial physical identity for each supported d. Fin.prod_univ_succ and associativity merely normalize the same four-factor order; no coefficient or factor is dropped.

The output evaluation uses Fin.snoc(cast ksMap y)(cast real norm(y)^2). The input evaluation uses the vector (ksSpinor y 0,ksSpinor y 1,star(ksSpinor y 0),star(ksSpinor y 1)). Both concern the same arbitrary y. There is no assumed arbitrary representative, independent radius, positive-degree hypothesis, or exclusion of y=0.

autoImplicit is false, and all three expanded declarations match the source. The balanced-support and row-degree requirements are explicit hypotheses, not proved from invariance here. The definition itself accepts every P; its interpretation as physical descent is only asserted under the displayed support condition. No missing invariant-support theorem is hidden in the statement.
